issue_context.title: Casting negative or large values to Time causes panic
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
>>> import polars as pl
>>> pl.Series([-1]).cast(pl.Time)
>>> pl.Series([86400000000000]).cast(pl.Time)
```


### Log output

```shell
NA
```


### Issue description

Values before 0:00 and after 24:00 are illegal for the Time type, but it appears that when casting Int32 to Time, the inclusion of these values causes panic.

### Expected behavior

Should not cause panic.

### Installed versions

<details>

```
--------Version info---------
Polars:              1.7.1
Index type:          UInt32
Platform:            Linux-5.15.153.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
Python:              3.10.12 (main, Jul 29 2024, 16:56:48) [GCC 11.4.0]
```

comments:
What is the right behavior? Time has limited range.
For instance what is the `pl.Time` value of `-1`?
It should be an error, for sure not a panic.

review_comments: I think we can use `to_arrow` which gives us the logical arrow type and then call the arrow `cast` kernels. Those should do these checks.
The `polars_arrow::compute::cast::cast` does not do these checks, if you are referring to that.
Then that kernel should. The casting behavior should be as much as possible in those kernels.
Okay, I will fix that then.
